title: Incomparability for an integral ring map
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $S$ is integral over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] (every element of $S$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\varphi(R)$). Let $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak q'$ be ideals of $S$ with $\mathfrak q$ prime. Then $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\subsetneq\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$. Equivalently: two distinct prime ideals of $S$ with the same inverse image in $R$ are incomparable (neither contains the other).
